<x_0.0029><y_0.0055>D MEASURES. 853<x_0.876><y_0.0281><class_Page-header>

<x_0.0371><y_0.0312>_Greece._-The same as in France.<x_0.4092><y_0.043><class_Text>

<x_0.7715><y_0.0344>Weights<x_0.8672><y_0.0453><class_Caption>

<x_0.0088><y_0.0414>_Guiana (British).--In general the same as in Britain; but the following, originally introduced by the Dutch, are also used: the lb. = 1•09 lbs. avoid. ; and the ell of 26 inches = 27 British inches.<x_0.7568><y_0.0852><class_Text>

<x_0.0107><y_0.0836>_Guiana_ (Dutch).--In general the same as in Holland, but chiefly upon the old system.<x_0.7539><y_0.107><class_Text>

<x_0.0098><y_0.1047>_Hamburg.--Of the weights, 128 drachmes = 32 loths = 16 oz._ = 2 marks = 1 lb. = 1•0682 lb. avoid. ; 112 lbs. = 8 lisponds = 1 centner = 119•64 lbs. avoid. ; and 5 centners = 2 shipfunds. Ten lbs. = 1 stone of wool or feathers = half a stone of flax. Of butter, 280 lbs. form the great, and 224 the small tonne. A pipe of oil is reckoned at 820 lbs. Gold and silver are weighed by the Cologne mark, and their fineness valued as explained under the head Germany. Of measures, 6 palms = 2 feet = 1 ell = 22•578 Brit. inches. The Rhinland foot of engineers and surveyors = 12•36 Brit. inches. The Brabant ell, commonly used for piece goods, = 27•585 Brit. inches. Also 160 quarters = 40 stubgens = 20 viertels = 5 elmers = 4 ankers = 1 ahm = 31•87 Brit. gall. ; and 24 ankers or 6 ahms = 1 fuder. Of wine, 6 tierces = 4 oxhofts or hogsheads = 1 faas; but these are of various sizes. Of corn, 160 spints = 40 himtens = 20 faas = 10 scheffels = 1 wisp or wispel = 29 Brit. bushels; two wisps = 1 last of barley or oats = 7•25 Brit. quarters; and 3 wisps = 1 last of wheat or rye = 1 stock of barley or cats = 10•87 Brit. quarters.<x_0.7588><y_0.2953><class_Text>

<x_0.0137><y_0.2938>_Hanover.--I'he lb. = 1•073 lb. avoid. ; 112 lbs. = 1 centner;_ and 20 lbs. = 1 stone of flax or 2 stones of wool. Also 600 lbs. = 51 stubgens = 2 tonnes of honey ; and 3360 lbs. = 240 lisponds = 12 shipfunds = 1 last. The Cologne mark is used for gold, silver, and silk. Two feet = 1 ell = 22•91 Brit. inches ; the mile = 6•5676 Brit. miles. The morgen land measure = 2•5625 Brit. roods. Also 80 kannen = 40 stubgens = 4 ankers = 2•5 elmers = 1 ahm = 34•24 Brit. gallons ; and 6 ahms = 4 oxhofts = 1 fuder of wine. Of corn, 96 himtens = 16 malters = 2 wisps or wispels = 1 last = 82 Brit. bushels.<x_0.7607><y_0.4><class_Text>

<x_0.0186><y_0.3984>_Hayti.--Port-au-Prince.--Principally the old system of France, together with the old English wine gallon._<x_0.7598><y_0.4219><class_Text>

<x_0.0195><y_0.4203>_Hese-Caretl.--The lb. = 17•08 oz. avoid. The ell = 22•59 Brit. inches ; the acre = ’5894 Brit. acre ; the liquid ohm = 34•94 Brit. gall. ; and 16 corn metzen = 4 himtens = 1 viertel = 4•42 Brit. bushels.<x_0.7617><y_0.4625><class_Text>

<x_0.0205><y_0.4617>_Hese-Darretadt.--Two lbs. = 1 French kilogramme = 2•20486_ lbs. avoid. Ten feet = 1 klafter = 2•5 metres = 8•2023 Brit. feet; five eils = 3 metres = 3•2809 Brit. yds. ; four morgens = 1 hec- tare = 2•47114 Brit. acres. The liquid ohm = 160 litres = 35•22 Brit. gallons ; the corn matter = 1•28 hectolitre = 3•522 Brit. bushels.<x_0.7627><y_0.5266><class_Text>

<x_0.0215><y_0.5242>_Holland.--In 1820, the decimal system of France was introdu- ed, but with the old Dutch nomenclature, as explained under the bead Belgium. Of the old weights still used in many places,_ 10,240 aas = 320 engels = 16 oz. = 2 marks = 1 Dutch lb. troy = 1•0851 lb. avoid. There are also 16 oz. in the commercial lb. = 1•0893 lb. avoid., and 100 commercial lbs. = 1 centner. The old Amsterdam foot = 11•15, and the ell = 27•08 Brit. inches; the Rhinland foot = 12•36, and the Flemish or Brabant ell = 27•58 Brit. inches. Nineteen Dutch leagues make one degree of the meridian.<x_0.7637><y_0.632><class_Text>

<x_0.0234><y_0.6281>_Japan.--The weights are almost the same as in China. The_ ine = 6•25 Brit. feet ; but the measures of capacity have not been compared.<x_0.7646><y_0.6641><class_Text>

<x_0.0225><y_0.6602>_Java.--In this and the other Dutch colonies in India, the weights_ of China are ordinarily employed ; but the pecul, instead of being exactly 133•33 lbs. avoid. is = 135•625 lbs. Of rice, the coyang = 3581 lbs. avoid. and the timbang = 10 sacks = 5 peculs = 678•125 lbs. The Dutch troy mark of 9 reals, = 3798 Brit. troy grains, is used for gold and silver. The foot = 12•36, and the ell = 27•75 Brit. inches. The kanne, liquid measure, = '3282 Brit. gall., and 396 rands = 1 leaguer of arrack = 133•33 Brit. gall. ; but 360 rands = 1 leaguer of wine.<x_0.7656><y_0.7586><class_Text>

<x_0.0254><y_0.7539>_India.--Grain is generally sold by weight, as also liquids, except wines and spirits, which at all the three presidencies are sold by British measures. Of the Bengal weights, 940 chittacks = 40 seers = 1 factory maund = 74•67 lbs. avoid. or two thirds of a British cwt. The bazaar maund is one tenth greater than the fac-tory, and similarly divided. Gold and silver are weighed by the new tola or sicea of 180 grains troy. Two cubits = 1 guz = 1 Brit. yd. The coss or mile of Bengal = 2000 yards, and 1600 sq. yds. = 20 cottabs = 1 biggah. At Bombay 40 seers = 1 maund = one quarter of a British cwt., and 20 maunds = 1 candy = 5 cwts., which in corn is counted at 24•5 Brit. bushels. At Madras, 320 pollams = 8 vis = 1 maund = 25 lbs. avoid., and 20 maunds = 1 candy. The covid = 18•6 inches, but the British yard is used for cloth ; and in land measure, 24 maunies = 1 cawney = 6400 Brit. sq. yds. Also 320 measures = 400 marals = 80 parahs = 1 garse<x_0.7695><y_0.918><class_Text>
